sanskrit: lohitākṣo mahābāhur ūrdhvakeśo mahābalaḥ meghasaṃghātavarṣmā ca tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrojjvalānanaḥ
english: Red-eyed, long-armed, hair erect, of great strength, his body massive as a mass of storm-clouds, his face blazing with sharp fangs —

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva tathā vikṛtadarśanam hiḍimbovāca vitrastā bhīmasenam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Seeing him rush toward them in so terrible a form, Hiḍimbā, trembling with fear, spoke these words to Bhīmasena:

sanskrit: āpataty eṣa duṣṭātmā saṃkruddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ tvām ahaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ yad bravīmi tathā kuru
english: "This evil-souled man-eater is rushing toward us in a fury. Do as I tell you — together with your brothers.

sanskrit: ahaṃ kāmagamā vīra rakṣobalasamanvitā āruhemāṃ mama śroṇīṃ neṣyāmi tvāṃ vihāyasā
english: I can go wherever I wish, hero, and I am endowed with the power of a rākṣasa. Climb onto my hips and I will carry you through the air.

sanskrit: prabodhayainān saṃsuptān mātaraṃ ca paraṃtapa sarvān eva gamiṣyāmi gṛhītvā vo vihāyasā
english: Wake those who are sleeping soundly, and your mother too, O scorcher of foes. Taking all of you, I will fly through the sky."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca mā bhais tvaṃ vipulaśroṇi naiṣa kaś cin mayi sthite aham enaṃ haniṣyāmi prekṣantyās te sumadhyame
english: Bhīma said: "Fear not, O broad-hipped one — while I stand here, this one is nothing. I will slay him before your very eyes, O slender-waisted lady.

sanskrit: nāyaṃ pratibalo bhīru rākṣasāpasado mama soḍhuṃ yudhi parispandam athavā sarvarākṣasāḥ
english: This wretch of a rākṣasa has not the power, O timid one, to withstand my onset in battle — nor indeed could all the rākṣasas combined.

sanskrit: paśya bāhū suvṛttau me hastihastanibhāv imau ūrū parighasaṃkāśau saṃhataṃ cāpy uro mama
english: Look at these two well-rounded arms of mine, like the trunks of elephants; at these thighs, like iron clubs; and at this compact chest of mine.

sanskrit: vikramaṃ me yathendrasya sādya drakṣyasi śobhane māvamaṃsthāḥ pṛthuśroṇi matvā mām iha mānuṣam
english: Today you shall see my valor equal to Indra's, O beautiful one. Do not despise me, O broad-hipped lady, thinking me a mere mortal."

sanskrit: hiḍimbovāca nāvamanye naravyāghra tvām ahaṃ devarūpiṇam dṛṣṭāpadānas tu mayā mānuṣeṣv eva rākṣasaḥ
english: Hiḍimbā said: "I do not despise you, O tiger among men — you are godlike in form. Yet the rākṣasa surpasses human beings even in the matter of footstep-speed."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā saṃjalpatas tasya bhīmasenasya bhārata vācaḥ śuśrāva tāḥ kruddho rākṣasaḥ puruṣādakaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as Bhīmasena was speaking thus, O Bhārata, the enraged man-eating rākṣasa heard those words.

sanskrit: avekṣamāṇas tasyāś ca hiḍimbo mānuṣaṃ vapuḥ sragdāmapūritaśikhaṃ samagrendunibhānanam
english: Hiḍimba observed his sister's human form — her hair adorned with garland-strands and wreaths, her face like the full moon,

sanskrit: subhrūnāsākṣikeśāntaṃ sukumāranakhatvacam sarvābharaṇasaṃyuktaṃ susūkṣmāmbaravāsasam
english: with beautiful brows, nose, eyes, and hair-ends, delicate nails and skin, decked in all ornaments, and clothed in the finest of garments.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ bibhratīṃ sumanoharam puṃskāmāṃ śaṅkamānaś ca cukrodha puruṣādakaḥ
english: Seeing her bearing that exceedingly beautiful human form and suspecting her of desire for a man, the man-eater flew into a rage.

sanskrit: saṃkruddho rākṣasas tasyā bhaginyāḥ kurusattama utphālya vipule netre tatas tām idam abravīt
english: The enraged rākṣasa, O best of the Kurus, rolling his great wide eyes at his sister, then spoke these words to her:

sanskrit: ko hi me bhoktukāmasya vighnaṃ carati durmatiḥ na bibheṣi hiḍimbe kiṃ matkopād vipramohitā
english: "Who is this fool who goes about obstructing me, eager as I am for my meal? Hiḍimbā, do you not fear my wrath? Are you so deluded?

sanskrit: dhik tvām asati puṃskāme mama vipriyakāriṇi pūrveṣāṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ sarveṣām ayaśaskari
english: Shame on you, wicked woman, lusting after a man, bringing dishonor upon me, and disgracing all our forebear chiefs among the rākṣasas!

sanskrit: yān imān āśritākārṣīr apriyaṃ sumahan mama eṣa tān adya vai sarvān haniṣyāmi tvayā saha
english: Those very men whom you have taken under your protection, doing me this great disservice — I shall slay all of them this day, along with you."

sanskrit: evam uktvā hiḍimbāṃ sa hiḍimbo lohitekṣaṇaḥ vadhāyābhipapātaināṃ dantair dantān upaspṛśan
english: Having said this, Hiḍimba with his blood-red eyes gnashed his teeth against his teeth and charged at Hiḍimbā to kill her.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ bhartsayām āsa tejasvī tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Seeing him rushing forward, Bhīma, the foremost of warriors, that spirited hero, checked him with threats and cried: "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bhīmasenas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ prahasann iva bhaginīṃ prati saṃkruddham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Bhīmasena, seeing the rākṣasa enraged against his sister, said with something like a laugh:

sanskrit: kiṃ te hiḍimba etair vā sukhasuptaiḥ prabodhitaiḥ mām āsādaya durbuddhe tarasā tvaṃ narāśana
english: "What do you want with those sleeping peacefully, Hiḍimba, whether woken or not? Come at me swiftly, O wicked-minded man-eater.

sanskrit: mayy eva praharaihi tvaṃ na striyaṃ hantum arhasi viśeṣato 'napakṛte pareṇāpakṛte sati
english: Strike at me alone — you ought not to slay a woman, especially one who has done you no harm, even if another has wronged you.

sanskrit: na hīyaṃ svavaśā bālā kāmayaty adya mām iha coditaiṣā hy anaṅgena śarīrāntaracāriṇā bhaginī tava durbuddhe rākṣasānāṃ yaśohara
english: This young woman is not of her own will desiring me here — she has been impelled by Kāma, who moves within the heart; she is your own sister, O wicked-minded disgrace of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tvanniyogena caiveyaṃ rūpaṃ mama samīkṣya ca kāmayaty adya māṃ bhīrur naiṣā dūṣayate kulam
english: Moreover, it was by your own command that she came here; having seen my form, this timid one desires me — she brings no disgrace upon the clan.

sanskrit: anaṅgena kṛte doṣe nemāṃ tvam iha rākṣasa mayi tiṣṭhati duṣṭātman na striyaṃ hantum arhasi
english: The fault was wrought by the bodiless one — while I stand here, you wicked-souled rākṣasa, you have no right to slay this woman.

sanskrit: samāgaccha mayā sārdham ekenaiko narāśana aham eva nayiṣyāmi tvām adya yamasādanam
english: Come and fight with me alone, one against one, O man-eater. Today I myself will conduct you to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: adya te talaniṣpiṣṭaṃ śiro rākṣasa dīryatām kuñjarasyeva pādena viniṣpiṣṭaṃ balīyasaḥ
english: Today let your head be crushed by my palm, O rākṣasa, split apart like a mighty elephant's foot crushing a skull.

sanskrit: adya gātrāṇi kravyādāḥ śyenā gomāyavaś ca te karṣantu bhuvi saṃhṛṣṭā nihatasya mayā mṛdhe
english: Today let the flesh-eating vultures, hawks, and jackals joyfully drag your limbs along the earth, slain by me in battle.

sanskrit: kṣaṇenādya kariṣye 'ham idaṃ vanam akaṇṭakam purastād dūṣitaṃ nityaṃ tvayā bhakṣayatā narān
english: In an instant today I shall make this forest free of its thorn — this forest that was forever befouled in the past by you devouring men.

sanskrit: adya tvāṃ bhaginī pāpa kṛṣyamāṇaṃ mayā bhuvi drakṣaty adripratīkāśaṃ siṃheneva mahādvipam
english: Today, O sinner, your sister shall see you dragged along the ground by me, mountain-like, as a lion drags a great elephant.

sanskrit: nirābādhās tvayi hate mayā rākṣasapāṃsana vanam etac cariṣyanti puruṣā vanacāriṇaḥ
english: With you slain by me, O disgrace of the rākṣasas, men who wander in forests will roam this forest free from all trouble."

sanskrit: hiḍimba uvāca garjitena vṛthā kiṃ te katthitena ca mānuṣa kṛtvaitat karmaṇā sarvaṃ katthethā mā ciraṃ kṛthāḥ
english: Hiḍimba said: "What is the use of roaring and boasting in vain, O mortal? Accomplish this deed and then boast of it all — do not delay long."

sanskrit: balinaṃ manyase yac ca ātmānam aparākramam jñāsyasy adya samāgamya mayātmānaṃ balādhikam
english: "You think yourself strong and me lacking in valor — today, when you close with me, you shall know your own strength to be the lesser."

sanskrit: na tāvad etān hiṃsiṣye svapantv ete yathāsukham eṣa tvām eva durbuddhe nihanmy adyāpriyaṃvadam
english: "I will not harm those sleeping there — let them sleep at their ease. It is you alone, O wicked-minded speaker of disagreeable words, that I slay today."

sanskrit: pītvā tavāsṛg gātrebhyas tataḥ paścād imān api haniṣyāmi tataḥ paścād imāṃ vipriyakāriṇīm
english: "After drinking your blood from your body, I will then slay them — and after that, this wretch who has done me harm."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tato bāhuṃ pragṛhya puruṣādakaḥ abhyadhāvata saṃkruddho bhīmasenam ariṃdamam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having said this, the man-eater seized his arm and charged in fury at Bhīmasena, the subduer of foes.

sanskrit: tasyābhipatatas tūrṇaṃ bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ vegena prahṛtaṃ bāhuṃ nijagrāha hasann iva
english: As he charged swiftly, Bhīma of terrible prowess caught the arm that had been thrust at him with a kind of laugh.

sanskrit: nigṛhya taṃ balād bhīmo visphurantaṃ cakarṣa ha tasmād deśād dhanūṃṣy aṣṭau siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: Seizing him forcibly, Bhīma dragged the writhing rākṣasa eight bow-lengths from that spot, as a lion drags a small beast.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rākṣasaḥ kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavena balād dhṛtaḥ bhīmasenaṃ samāliṅgya vyanadad bhairavaṃ ravam
english: Then the rākṣasa, enraged, held fast by the Pāṇḍava, clasped Bhīmasena in his arms and let out a dreadful roar.

sanskrit: punar bhīmo balād enaṃ vicakarṣa mahābalaḥ mā śabdaḥ sukhasuptānāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ me bhaved iti
english: Again mighty Bhīma forcibly dragged him away, thinking: "Let there be no noise to wake my brothers who are sleeping soundly."

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ tau samāsādya vicakarṣatur ojasā rākṣaso bhīmasenaś ca vikramaṃ cakratuḥ param
english: The two of them, coming at each other, dragged one another with all their might — the rākṣasa and Bhīmasena each displaying supreme valor.

sanskrit: babhañjatur mahāvṛkṣāṃl latāś cākarṣatus tataḥ mattāv iva susaṃrabdhau vāraṇau ṣaṣṭihāyanau
english: They broke great trees and tore apart creepers, like two sixty-year-old elephants in rut, both fiercely enraged.

sanskrit: tayoḥ śabdena mahatā vibuddhās te nararṣabhāḥ saha mātrā tu dadṛśur hiḍimbām agrataḥ sthitām
english: Roused by the great noise the two made, those bulls among men awoke along with their mother — and they saw Hiḍimbā standing before them.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prabuddhās te hiḍimbāyā rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvātimānuṣam vismitāḥ puruṣavyāghrā babhūvuḥ pṛthayā saha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Awakened and seeing Hiḍimbā's superhuman form, those tigers among men were filled with wonder, as was Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuntī samīkṣyaināṃ vismitā rūpasaṃpadā uvāca madhuraṃ vākyaṃ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ śanaiḥ
english: Then Kuntī, marveling at her beauty, spoke these sweet soothing words to her gently:

sanskrit: kasya tvaṃ suragarbhābhe kā cāsi varavarṇini kena kāryeṇa suśroṇi kutaś cāgamanaṃ tava
english: "Whose are you, O one radiant as the womb of the gods? Who are you, O lady of fine complexion? What is your purpose here, O beautiful-hipped one? And from where have you come?

sanskrit: yadi vāsya vanasyāsi devatā yadi vāpsarāḥ ācakṣva mama tat sarvaṃ kimarthaṃ ceha tiṣṭhasi
english: Whether you are a deity of this forest or an Apsaras, tell me everything — and for what purpose do you stand here?"

sanskrit: hiḍimbovāca yad etat paśyasi vanaṃ nīlameghanibhaṃ mahat nivāso rākṣasasyaitad dhiḍimbasya mamaiva ca
english: Hiḍimbā said: "This great forest you see, dark as a rain-cloud — this is the dwelling place of the rākṣasa Hiḍimba, and of me as well.

sanskrit: tasya māṃ rākṣasendrasya bhaginīṃ viddhi bhāmini bhrātrā saṃpreṣitām ārye tvāṃ saputrāṃ jighāṃsatā
english: Know me, O spirited lady, as the sister of that rākṣasa lord — sent by my brother, O noble one, who wished to kill you along with your sons.

sanskrit: krūrabuddher ahaṃ tasya vacanād āgatā iha adrākṣaṃ hemavarṇābhaṃ tava putraṃ mahaujasam
english: Acting on the orders of that cruel-minded one, I came here and beheld your son, golden-complexioned and of great splendor.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ bhāve vicaratā śubhe coditā tava putrasya manmathena vaśānugā
english: Then I, wandering in the nature of all beings, was impelled by Manmatha who had entered your son — I came under his sway, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: tato vṛto mayā bhartā tava putro mahābalaḥ apanetuṃ ca yatito na caiva śakito mayā
english: So I chose your mighty son as my husband, and tried to carry him away — but I could not.

sanskrit: cirāyamāṇāṃ māṃ jñātvā tataḥ sa puruṣādakaḥ svayam evāgato hantum imān sarvāṃs tavātmajān
english: Knowing that I was delaying, that man-eater has himself come here to slay all your sons.

sanskrit: sa tena mama kāntena tava putreṇa dhīmatā balād ito viniṣpiṣya vyapakṛṣṭo mahātmanā
english: He has been forcibly crushed and dragged away from here by that wise great-souled one, your son, my beloved.

sanskrit: vikarṣantau mahāvegau garjamānau parasparam paśyadhvaṃ yudhi vikrāntāv etau tau nararākṣasau
english: Behold those two of mighty speed roaring at each other — the man and the rākṣasa, both displaying valor in battle!"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasyāḥ śrutvaiva vacanam utpapāta yudhiṣṭhiraḥ arjuno nakulaś caiva sahadevaś ca vīryavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The moment they heard her words, Yudhiṣṭhira, Arjuna, and valiant Nakula and Sahadeva leapt to their feet.

sanskrit: tau te dadṛśur āsaktau vikarṣantau parasparam kāṅkṣamāṇau jayaṃ caiva siṃhāv iva raṇotkaṭau
english: They saw the two locked together, dragging each other, each striving for victory, like two lions fierce in battle.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ samāśliṣya vikarṣantau parasparam dāvāgnidhūmasadṛśaṃ cakratuḥ pārthivaṃ rajaḥ
english: The two of them, clasping each other and dragging back and forth, raised a cloud of dust from the earth like the smoke of a forest fire.

sanskrit: vasudhāreṇusaṃvītau vasudhādharasaṃnibhau vibhrājetāṃ yathā śailau nīhāreṇābhisaṃvṛtau
english: Enveloped in the dust of the earth, resembling the pillars of the earth itself, the two blazed like two mountains wrapped in mist.

sanskrit: rākṣasena tathā bhīmaṃ kliśyamānaṃ nirīkṣya tu uvācedaṃ vacaḥ pārthaḥ prahasañ śanakair iva
english: Watching Bhīma being hard pressed by the rākṣasa, Arjuna spoke these words with something of a laugh:

sanskrit: bhīma mā bhair mahābāho na tvāṃ budhyāmahe vayam sametaṃ bhīmarūpeṇa prasuptāḥ śramakarśitāḥ
english: "Fear not, Bhīma, O great-armed one — we did not know you had met this fearsome form while we slept, wearied and worn out.

sanskrit: sāhāyye 'smi sthitaḥ pārtha yodhayiṣyāmi rākṣasam nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca mātaraṃ gopayiṣyataḥ
english: I am here to aid you, O son of Pṛthā — I will fight the rākṣasa. Nakula and Sahadeva shall guard our mother."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca udāsīno nirīkṣasva na kāryaḥ saṃbhramas tvayā na jātv ayaṃ punar jīven madbāhvantaram āgataḥ
english: Bhīma said: "Stand aside and watch — no alarm is needed from you. This one, having come within the reach of my arms, shall never live again."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kim anena ciraṃ bhīma jīvatā pāparakṣasā gantavyaṃ na ciraṃ sthātum iha śakyam ariṃdama
english: Arjuna said: "Why keep this sinful rākṣasa alive so long, Bhīma? We cannot linger here much longer, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: purā saṃrajyate prācī purā saṃdhyā pravartate raudre muhūrte rakṣāṃsi prabalāni bhavanti ca
english: Before long the east will redden; before long the twilight will begin; and at the dreadful hour, rākṣasas grow powerful.

sanskrit: tvarasva bhīma mā krīḍa jahi rakṣo vibhīṣaṇam purā vikurute māyāṃ bhujayoḥ sāram arpaya
english: Hurry, Bhīma — do not play games. Slay this fearsome demon before he works his magic; pour the essence of your arms into this."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca arjunenaivam uktas tu bhīmo bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ utkṣipyābhrāmayad dehaṃ tūrṇaṃ guṇaśatādhikam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus urged by Arjuna, Bhīma quickly lifted the dreadful rākṣasa's body and whirled it round more than a hundred times.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca vṛthāmāṃsair vṛthā puṣṭo vṛthā vṛddho vṛthāmatiḥ vṛthāmaraṇam arhas tvaṃ vṛthādya na bhaviṣyasi
english: Bhīma said: "Nourished on flesh in vain, grown up in vain, your mind wasted in vain — you deserve a futile death; today your futility will come to an end."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca atha vā manyase bhāraṃ tvam imaṃ rākṣasaṃ yudhi karomi tava sāhāyyaṃ śīghram eva nihanyatām
english: Arjuna said: "Or if you think this rākṣasa too heavy a burden in battle, I will help you — let him be slain quickly."

sanskrit: atha vāpy aham evainaṃ haniṣyāmi vṛkodara kṛtakarmā pariśrāntaḥ sādhu tāvad upārama
english: "Or I myself will slay him, O wolf-belly — you have done great deeds and are exhausted. Do take rest for a while."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ niṣpiṣyainaṃ balād bhūmau paśumāram amārayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those words, the exceedingly wrathful Bhīmasena crushed the rākṣasa forcibly against the earth and killed him like a sacrificial animal.

sanskrit: sa māryamāṇo bhīmena nanāda vipulaṃ svanam pūrayaṃs tad vanaṃ sarvaṃ jalārdra iva dundubhiḥ
english: As he was being killed by Bhīma, he let out a great loud cry that filled the entire forest, like a drum soaked in water.

sanskrit: bhujābhyāṃ yoktrayitvā taṃ balavān pāṇḍunandanaḥ madhye bhaṅktvā sa balavān harṣayām āsa pāṇḍavān
english: That powerful son of Pāṇḍu, wrapping him with his arms, broke him at the waist — and that mighty hero delighted the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: hiḍimbaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃhṛṣṭās te tarasvinaḥ apūjayan naravyāghraṃ bhīmasenam ariṃdamam
english: Seeing Hiḍimba slain, those swift heroes rejoiced and honored Bhīmasena, that tiger among men, that subduer of foes.

sanskrit: abhipūjya mahātmānaṃ bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramam punar evārjuno vākyam uvācedaṃ vṛkodaram
english: Having duly honored the great-souled Bhīma of terrible valor, Arjuna again spoke these words to that wolf-bellied one:

sanskrit: nadūre nagaraṃ manye vanād asmād ahaṃ prabho śīghraṃ gacchāma bhadraṃ te na no vidyāt suyodhanaḥ
english: "I think a city is not far from this forest, lord. Let us go quickly — good fortune to you. Let Suyodhana not find us out."

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve tathety uktvā saha mātrā paraṃtapāḥ prayayuḥ puruṣavyāghrā hiḍimbā caiva rākṣasī
english: Then all of them, those scorchers of foes, those tigers among men, said "So be it" and departed along with their mother — and Hiḍimbā the rākṣasī went with them.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca smaranti vairaṃ rakṣāṃsi māyām āśritya mohinīm hiḍimbe vraja panthānaṃ tvaṃ vai bhrātṛniṣevitam
english: Bhīma said: "Rākṣasas remember enmity and resort to bewildering illusion, Hiḍimbā — go you on the path trodden by your brother."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kruddho 'pi puruṣavyāghra bhīma mā sma striyaṃ vadhīḥ śarīraguptyābhyadhikaṃ dharmaṃ gopaya pāṇḍava
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Even in your anger, O tiger among men, Bhīma, do not slay a woman — guard dharma, which is greater than protecting the body. Guard it, O Pāṇḍava."
